§11.2.8 Scatter and Error Bars

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-scatter-and-error-bars · charts types

✅ Normative

A named scatter point MUST be rendered as one row holding its x value and its y value. Marker series over categories are ordinary series columns. An error bar's centre is an ordinary value, and its whisker span MUST be given with it: the low and high ends read at the whisker caps. A box plot MUST give its median, first and third quartiles, and its whisker ends when they are drawn. Points with no printed name have nothing to locate them and are not rendered as rows.

Scatter

Each named dot contributes its two coordinates, each read against its own axis (see Values and Tolerances§11.1.4). A fitted trend line through the cloud is reference ink (see Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3).

How scatter points, whiskers and boxes appear in the chart table.

  • A scatter chart MUST give one row per named point, a column for x and a column for y, each headed by its printed axis title.
  • An error bar's interval MUST be written in the centre's cell, after the centre, as centre (low–high) — 3.60 (3.47–3.73).
  • A box plot MUST give one row per box: its label, then the low whisker end, first quartile, median, third quartile and high whisker end in axis order, the whisker ends only where drawn, under the header row Low | Q1 | Median | Q3 | High (first cell: the printed label column's title, or empty). These header cells are protocol vocabulary, like the markers [blank] or [logo: …]: the page does not print them, and they are the one deliberate exception to never invent, so that the columns can be read without guessing. They are written exactly as given.

✅ Sample (constructed) — make_scatter

Ten named points, one row each, x and y under the two printed axis titles. The plotted values are whole numbers by construction; on a printed page they would be estimates, judged with a tolerance.

Dot and marker series over categories

Dots drawn per category — markers above bars, one marker per gender per country — are ordinary series: one column per marker series, one value per mark.

Error bars

The centre is copied when printed and estimated otherwise. The whisker ends are read at the caps against the axis, like any estimate. A whisker whose ends cannot be read honestly is not given an interval.

A checker judges the interval on meaning: it accepts any output that conveys it — 3.60 ± 0.13, 3.60 (3.47–3.73), separate low and high columns, prose — within the tolerance of an ordinary estimate, and fails a centre given with no interval.

✅ Sample — db242_p2


Source: CDC/NCHS, National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2009–2012 — Figure 2 (public domain)

Six bars printing their means, with footnote markers, and 95% confidence whiskers drawn but not printed. Each cell holds the printed centre, markers included, followed by the whisker ends read against the 0.50 grid. The dashed Adequate intake lines are reference ink: their labels follow the table as text. The whisker symbol before 95% confidence interval. is not text.

Panel (c) shows its first three bars, then the rest; its two bracket captions follow its table as text. The page heading and the figure caption below the panels are elided.

✅ Sample — ac8b3538-en_p131

Five bars with confidence whiskers, nothing printed: five rows, negatives included, each with its interval. The whisker ends are read at the drawn caps against the printed axis. The GHG-intensive occupations bar sits almost on zero: a relative tolerance means little there, so a checker widens it (0.3) rather than tightening the reading.

Box plots

A box's median, quartiles and drawn whisker ends are read from the geometry. Statistics printed beside the plot are text on the page and are copied as printed.

✅ Sample — charpy_verification_p24

Two box plots, both over the category HH-103, each its own table under its own figure caption, which tells them apart. Each box gives five readings against its axis; the printed annotation box and the labels of the dashed outlier-limit lines follow the table as text. The individual test values (crosses) and the mean marker carry no name and are not rows.
